# Wire vector provenance

These are synthetic, bounded standards-conformance examples authored on
2026-09-26 against the public v3 schemas at repository revision
`621ffc6727ebe626e098b96b33e0c1a9431b43ef`. Their inputs and expectations use
only the public schemas and published protobuf rules.

Each `hex` body was assembled from the documented protobuf field tags, wire
types, lengths, and primitive encodings. Its `expected_semantics` object was
authored independently. Neither the Prost encoder nor its decoded output was
used to create the input bytes or expected result. The numerical page's noun
shape and each request's noun shape are explicit, readable `canonical_nouns`
expectations; they are not generated through the conversion under test.

The governing public references are the protobuf
[encoding rules](https://protobuf.dev/programming-guides/encoding/), including
duplicate fields and packed fields; the proto3
[oneof rules](https://protobuf.dev/programming-guides/proto3/#oneof-features),
[unknown-field rules](https://protobuf.dev/programming-guides/proto3/#unknowns),
and [enum rules](https://protobuf.dev/programming-guides/proto3/#enum); and
[ProtoJSON representation](https://protobuf.dev/programming-guides/json/).

The independent reference is Google's Python protobuf runtime **7.36.2**, with
Python modules generated by **protoc 36.2** from the fixed public repository
schemas. `MessageToDict(..., preserving_proto_field_name=True)` defines the
semantic comparison: uint64/fixed64 values are decimal strings, bytes are
base64, known enums use names, and unknown enums retain their integer number.
Explicit optional and oneof zero values remain present. Unknown fields are
outside this JSON projection.

To reproduce from the repository root, install protoc 36.2 and run:

```sh
python3 -m venv .venv-peer-v3-conformance
.venv-peer-v3-conformance/bin/python -m pip install -r scripts/peer-v3-conformance-requirements.txt
.venv-peer-v3-conformance/bin/python scripts/peer-v3-conformance.py
cargo test -p nockchain-libp2p-io --lib v3::wire_tests
```

The runner checks tool versions and generates Python code in a disposable
directory. It does not use protobuf reserialization as an expected oracle.
All 23 authored semantic objects matched the independent reference without
adjusting expectations to agree with either parser.

The two numeric-page cases use the public hash tuple `[1 0 0 0 0]`. Its
nonempty base58 identity satisfies the response-envelope domain; the zero
hash would have an empty identity and fail that check. These are synthetic
representation fixtures, not consensus-accepted blocks.

To extend the corpus, author the raw hex and semantic/noun expectations from
the relevant schema and published rule, add the requirement to the coverage
matrix, then run both implementations. Review the fixture diff explicitly.
There is no command that blesses the implementation's current output as the
new expectation. A change in parser behavior must be investigated before any
expected result changes.
